# Challenge corpus

Independent probes for detection forms the main corpus structurally cannot
produce.

## Why this exists

`tests/fixtures/synthetic_cn_notes/` is generated by
`tools/generate_synthetic_cn_notes.py`, whose templates are written to match
detector capabilities. A strict 1.0 there measures agreement with those
templates, not real-world generalisation — `docs/scope.md` states this
explicitly. When the detector and the corpus share an author and a vocabulary, a
blind spot is invisible in both.

This directory holds samples produced independently of that generator and of the
detector regexes.

## Layout

- `regression/` — forms that are fixed today. Runs in CI and must pass.
- `exploratory/` — forms that are not covered. Reported separately and expected
  to contain failures. Not run in CI.

## Format

Each probe is a `.txt` file plus a `.probes.json` sidecar:

```json
{
  "doc_id": "narrative_001",
  "dimension": "narrative",
  "expected_verdict": "SANITIZE",
  "must_detect": [{"type": "PERSON_NAME", "text": "李四"}],
  "must_not_detect": ["本病区"]
}
```

`must_detect` entries are matched by fact type and exact text. `must_not_detect`
entries assert that a substring is not reported as any fact type — the
over-redaction direction, which the main benchmark measures only in aggregate.

## What is measured

Per dimension and separately: how many probes reached their expected verdict,
how many `must_detect` entries were found, and how many `must_not_detect` entries
were violated. **No aggregate score is produced.** A single number can hide a
dimension that fails entirely behind one that passes.

## What is not measured

- Real patient data. Every probe is synthetic.
- Adversarial evasion (zero-width characters, homoglyphs, deliberate splitting).
  `docs/scope.md` lists "preventing intentional bypass by actors that already
  hold raw PHI" as a non-goal; including it here would misdirect priorities.
- Anything the dimensions do not name. The absence of a probe is not evidence of
  coverage.

## Dimensions

| Dimension | Probes | Status |
|---|---|---|
| narrative | 10 regression / 4 exploratory | names in varied syntactic positions |

### narrative

Regression probes cover forms the baseline handles: the adjacent field form
(`患者` + surname + clinical verb), compound surnames, the `姓名，性别` narrative
opener, labelled controls, and two over-redaction controls where an ordinary
word must not be read as a name.

Exploratory probes are bare names with no field label at all (`李四因胸痛入院。`).
`detectors/person.py` deliberately does not detect bare name tokens — the
false-positive rate on free text would be unacceptable — so these are expected
to fail. They are recorded rather than asserted.

One consequence of the adjacent form is worth stating plainly: it now requires
the given name to come from the name-character inventory in
`detectors/surnames.py`. A real name whose given character is outside that
inventory is not detected. That is the price of not reading `患者周转正常` as a
person called 周转正常.

## Relationship to the main benchmark

Separate directory, separate command, separate report. Challenge results must
not be cited as evidence for the 175-document corpus, nor the reverse.
